Other exported activities (UriHandler, MainActivity, FilterSelectionActivity, widget/Tasker config) only show UI to the user or return user-selected values.

The other exported receivers only react to system actions (boot, package replaced, provider change, widget update) by refreshing state.

evidence.detail: FireReceiver exported with no android:permission.
Package check is satisfiable by any sender via setPackage().

fills.reason: Reminder notifications show the task title and description (user-authored content) with no setVisibility/public version, so they appear on the lock screen per system settings; minSdk is 26. Whether task contents count as sensitive data for this app is a product decision.

The only shared-storage API is getExternalFilesDir (app-specific dir for backups), and no WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE/MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE permission is declared; MediaStore is only used as intent actions for camera/recorder/picker.
Android encryption uses a key generated inside AndroidKeyStore (AndroidKeyProvider); the only SecretKeySpec is in the desktop-only DesktopKeyProvider, not in Android source sets.
The only Cipher used is AES/GCM/NoPadding; no DES, 3DES, RC4 or Blowfish anywhere in Android code.
Cipher transformation is AES/GCM/NoPadding with a random 12-byte IV per encryption; no ECB or bare "AES".
The AndroidKeyStore AES key protecting stored account passwords is generated without setKeySize, so it uses the keystore default of 128 bits, which this test treats as insufficient.

evidence.detail: KeyGenParameterSpec built with no setKeySize (defaults to AES-128).

fills.reason: java.util.Random is used only for random reminder times (AlarmCalculator) and job start jitter (WorkManagerImpl); PKCE verifiers, nonces and IVs use SecureRandom.
Security values (OAuth PKCE verifier/nonce/state, GCM IV) come from SecureRandom; no time-based generation of tokens found.
The only provider-qualified getInstance calls use AndroidKeyStore (KeyStore and KeyGenerator); Cipher, MessageDigest and SSLContext use the default provider.
No asymmetric key pairs are generated (no KeyPairGenerator); the single keystore key is a symmetric AES key limited to ENCRYPT|DECRYPT.
No KeyguardManager.isDeviceSecure/isKeyguardSecure or BiometricManager.canAuthenticate call exists anywhere in the app, so it never checks for a secure screen lock before storing credentials.

evidence.detail: Credential-protecting key created without any device-lock check in the app.

Internal broadcasts go through androidx LocalBroadcastManager (in-process) or explicit component intents (CompleteTaskReceiver, TasksWidget); internal startActivity intents name their class.
Intents carrying extras (task ids, filters, widget ids) are explicit or in-process local broadcasts; no implicit intent with credentials or tokens was found.

Every PendingIntent wraps an explicit intent. FLAG_IMMUTABLE is used except where mutability is required by the API: widget fill-in template, requestPinAppWidget callback (receives the widget id), geofence/location update broadcasts, and the AppAuth completion intent.
No intent-filter declares an http/https data scheme; https appears only inside <queries>. Deep links use custom schemes (OAuth redirects, msauth) and content://.

The custom-scheme handlers are library activities (AppAuth RedirectUriReceiverActivity, MSAL BrowserTabActivity) whose state/parameter validation lives in the libraries, not in this project; the app's own UriHandler handles only content:// URIs and parses ids with toLongOrNull.
SSLContext.getInstance("TLS") uses platform defaults; no setEnabledProtocols, ConnectionSpec or tlsVersions configuration enabling old TLS.
The only http:// strings in Android code are XML namespace identifiers (CalDAV properties) and the loopback OAuth redirect http://127.0.0.1:port, which doesn't leave the device.
No direct SSLSocket use; TLS goes through OkHttp/Ktor with a HostnameVerifier set (OkHostnameVerifier wrapped by cert4android).

OkHttp clients use cert4android's custom X509TrustManager, which accepts any certificate stored as 'trusted by user', bypassing system/NSC validation. That trust store can be written by any app through the exported TrustCertificateActivity's EXTRA_TRUSTED path, so an attacker-chosen certificate can become trusted.

evidence.detail: Any user-trusted cert short-circuits chain validation.
Custom trust manager installed for all OkHttp clients.
Trust decision reachable from other apps via exported activity.
